title: Mix, Don’t Tune: Bilingual Pre-Training Outperforms Hyperparameter Search in Data-Constrained Settings
gist: Across about 1000 pre-training runs at 150M to 1.43B parameters with Arabic as target and English as auxiliary, mixing in a high-resource language beat aggressive hyperparameter tuning, with the gap growing with model size. Mixing was worth 2-3x unique target data on validation loss and 2-13x on downstream accuracy.

insights.claim: For most of the world's languages, LM pre-training is data-constrained, forcing models to repeat training data many times and degrading generalization.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Data scarcity, not compute, limits non-English models, creating room for data-efficiency techniques.
insights.locator: For most languages of the world

insights.claim: Two remedies exist: aggressive hyperparameter tuning such as high weight decay, which regularizes by restricting capacity, and mixing in high-resource auxiliary-language data, which expands the training distribution.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames the design choice between regularizing and adding new knowledge.

insights.claim: In about 1000 runs across four scales from 150M to 1.43B parameters, mixing yields larger improvements than hyperparameter tuning on both validation loss and downstream accuracy, and the gap grows with model size.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Benefits increase with scale, so the advantage should matter more for larger multilingual models.
insights.locator: mixing yields larger improvements than hyperparameter tuning

insights.claim: Mixing boosts performance by an amount equivalent to 2-3x the unique target data on validation loss and 2-13x on downstream task accuracy, with gains scaling steeply with model size.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Mixing acts like a multiplier on scarce target-language data, lowering the cost of building low-resource models.
insights.locator: 2–3× the unique target data on validation loss

insights.claim: Target-language validation loss systematically underestimates the value of mixing, since mixing both regularizes by diversifying the signal and contributes knowledge the repeated target corpus cannot supply, and validation loss captures only the first.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Relying on validation loss alone can lead to wrong data-mix decisions; downstream evals matter.
insights.locator: validation loss captures only the first effect

insights.claim: The authors recommend mixing in a high-resource language, prioritizing the mixing ratio over hyperparameter tuning, and transferring hyperparameters from a small proxy model via muP.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Cheaper training recipe: small-proxy tuning plus data mix, reducing expensive large-scale search.

insights.claim: Related Apple work extends muP-style transfer of optimal global hyperparameters from small to large models, noting hyperparameters strongly affect training stability and final performance.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Hyperparameter transfer cuts the compute spent on large-run tuning.
insights.locator: Recent works on neural network parameterisations

insights.claim: Related Apple work notes that fine-tuning on limited target data quickly overfits and drifts away from the original model, forgetting pre-training knowledge.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Domain adaptation has known failure modes that motivate mixing-style approaches.
